To compare two models, choose “Against another value model” (two MCTS at one table); the result is recorded only on the model chosen above, the other model's records do not change.

hp.what.body:
Every **dataset**, **model** and **match** has a **hash** (SHA-256; the screen shows the first 8 characters): the “parameters that decide the result” put in a fixed form and hashed. The engine is deterministic for a config and seed, so **the hash is the same only when all parameters are the same, and running again gives the same content**; any different parameter gives a different hash.

A hash only answers “is everything the same”; “what differs” is found by comparing the recorded parameters (for example “Games: 20,000 → 200,000”).
hp.what.note: Normal form: parameter names sorted, `100` and `100.0` count as equal, seat order is case-insensitive. The computation is in `ml/fingerprint.py`.
hp.model.note: When a training parameter is added, `fingerprint.LGBM_OPTIONS` / `MLP_OPTIONS` must be updated too (a test checks it). Early backfilled models have no hash and are marked “old record”.
hp.mlp_extra: ; the training engine and device use the **resolved** values (auto becomes torch/numpy, cuda/cpu)
hp.match.body: Same as data (players, games, seed, seat order, each seat's strategy, strategy version and full parameters, value-model file content, limits, options, rule set and rules version, variant), but **without** the sampling rate and feature version. Not counted: result file name, config name, seat id, threads, engine version and git commit. Every match also records the hash of the model file at the time: if the model is overwritten later, the old result is marked “model file updated”.
hp.versions.card: Rules version, strategy versions and defaults
hp.versions.body:
- **Rules version** (currently {now}): bumped only when the game rules or the randomness / seed derivation change; all data is affected.
- **Strategy version** (for example `harbor-rush-v1`): bumped only when that strategy's own decision logic changes; **only data that uses that strategy** is affected; MCTS's version also covers its rollout strategy and the value-model inference code.
- **Defaults**: changing a strategy's default parameters does **not** need a version. The engine records every seat's full parameters (defaults filled in) in data and result files, and the hash uses them, so a changed default naturally changes the hash.
- **Old files**: data and result files from before the engine recorded full parameters are completed from a frozen defaults table (`ml/strategy-params.legacy.json`, the defaults of strategy v1 and rules base-v1 at the time); later default changes do not affect them. New runs predict their hash from the current defaults table (`ml/strategy-params.json`, produced by the engine and checked against the code by a test).
hp.use.card: How the ML UI uses hashes
hp.use.body:
- **Same name**: same hash → “identical, no need to overwrite”; different → the differences are listed; data used by models lists which models.
- **Different name, same hash**: flagged as a duplicate (so the same data is not ticked twice for training, which would show the model the same positions twice).
- **Old versions**: when the rules version is below the current one ({now}), or a seat's strategy version is below the current one in data and models, “Version status” says “Old: …” and regenerating is recommended.
- **Queue protection**: files a queued or running job will read (training data, models used in matches) cannot be overwritten.

pl.intro: Build a whole run: generate data → train models → validate them with matches. Each “Add” button opens a window to set one item up; added items are listed with their details (read-only: to change one, remove it and add it again). Everything is queued as one pipeline: the jobs run in this order — all the data first, then each model followed by its own matches — and later jobs can use the data and models that earlier jobs are about to produce. When any job fails or is cancelled, the jobs of the pipeline that have not started are cancelled too (files already written stay).
